fatal_errors: The hypothesis concerns HfNbTiVAl10 tensile and fracture-property prediction, whereas the target study concerns composition screening and experimental validation in the Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W system.
It fails to reconstruct the screening of 38,326 compositions using rule-of-mixtures modulus, VEC, and density or the selection of Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5.
It substitutes tensile and fracture-toughness testing for the target's room-temperature quasi-static compression experiments.
The claimed 15–20% accuracy improvement and tenfold speedup have no cited evidence, defined error metric, dataset, or measured comparator.
No supporting prior evidence is identified.
The proposed model predicts fracture toughness despite no specified toughness definition, specimen geometry, crack preparation, or validated toughness labels.
explanation: This is a generic, potentially testable physics-informed GNN proposal rather than a reconstruction of the target work. It misses the material system, selected composition, composition-only screening method, VEC/dislocation-mobility mechanism, as-cast compression conditions, equimolar NbMoTaVW baseline, and reported strength–ductility results. Its boundary discussion appropriately notes descriptor availability, out-of-distribution microstructures, and test-condition shifts, but remains generic. The blinded prospective concept provides some discriminability, yet it lacks sample numbers, fixed train/test separation, exact ASTM methods, predefined error metrics and confidence intervals, and a rigorous runtime baseline. Consequently, the quantitative gains are speculative and unsupported.
